from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("What is a Vector?", ["Scalars have only magnitude.", "Vectors add direction to magnitude.", "Vectors act like arrows in space."])
        
        # Define colors for lecture lines
        COLOR_SCALAR = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_VECTOR_V = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_VECTOR_U = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display an arrow on screen. Color: #FFFFFF. Label: 'Vector v'.
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color=COLOR_SCALAR)
        label1 = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=COLOR_SCALAR).next_to(arrow1, UP)
        v_group1 = VGroup(arrow1, label1)
        self.place_at_grid(v_group1, 'C4')
        self.play(Create(v_group1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_SCALAR)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the arrow moving from the origin. Color: #FF00FF. Label: 'Vector v'.
        self.play(v_group1.animate.set_color(COLOR_VECTOR_V),
                  label1.animate.set_color(COLOR_VECTOR_V))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_VECTOR_V)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display a second identical vector alongside. Color: #00FFFF. Label: 'Vector u'.
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color=COLOR_VECTOR_U)
        label2 = MathTex(r"\vec{u}", color=COLOR_VECTOR_U).next_to(arrow2, UP)
        v_group2 = VGroup(arrow2, label2)
        self.place_at_grid(v_group2, 'E4')
        self.play(Create(v_group2))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_VECTOR_U)
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Vector Addition", ["Place vectors tip-to-tail.", "The resultant connects start to finish.", "Addition is commutative."])
        
        # Colors: #00FFFF, #FF00FF, #FFFF00
        # Mobjects
        u = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00FFFF")
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#FF00FF")
        
        label_u = MathTex("u", color="#00FFFF")
        label_v = MathTex("v", color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Placement
        self.place_at_grid(u, 'D4')
        label_u.next_to(u, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'D5')
        label_v.next_to(v, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show vectors u and v head-to-tail
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(u), Write(label_u))
        
        v_shifted = v.copy().shift(u.get_end())
        label_v_shifted = label_v.copy().next_to(v_shifted, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v_shifted), Write(label_v_shifted))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The resultant connects start to finish.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        resultant = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=u.get_end() + v_shifted.get_vector(), color="#FFFF00")
        label_resultant = MathTex("u + v", color="#FFFF00").next_to(resultant.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(label_resultant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Addition is commutative.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Animate u sliding to connect to v
        u_shifted = u.copy().shift(v_shifted.get_end() - u.get_end())
        self.play(FadeOut(u), FadeOut(label_u))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(u.copy(), u_shifted))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Components of a Vector", ["Break vectors into x and y.", "Use i and j basis units.", "Combine them to form vectors."])
        
        # Grid
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 7, 1], y_range=[-1, 5, 1], 
                           axis_config={"include_numbers": False, "stroke_color": "#333333"})
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(grid)

        # Define vector
        origin = self.grid["F1"]
        end = self.grid["C4"]
        vec_v = Arrow(origin, end, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        label_v = Text("v", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(vec_v.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(vec_v), Write(label_v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Projections
        vx = Line(origin, [end[0], origin[1], 0], color="#FF0000", stroke_width=4)
        vy = Line([end[0], origin[1], 0], end, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        label_vx = Text("vx", font_size=20, color="#FF0000")
        label_vx.next_to(vx.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        label_vy = Text("vy", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        label_vy.next_to(vy.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(vx), Create(vy), Write(label_vx), Write(label_vy))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Indicate(vec_v))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors model motion and space.", "They power physics engines.", "Fundamental to modern navigation."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color constants
        COLOR_1 = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_2 = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_3 = "#00FFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a collection of vectors together
        vectors = VGroup(*[
            Vector(direction=RIGHT*0.5 + UP*0.5, color=COLOR_1).shift(self.grid["B3"]),
            Vector(direction=LEFT*0.3 + UP*0.6, color=COLOR_1).shift(self.grid["B5"]),
            Vector(direction=DOWN*0.4 + RIGHT*0.2, color=COLOR_1).shift(self.grid["D4"]),
        ])
        label1 = Text("Set of Vectors", font_size=20, color=COLOR_1)
        label1.next_to(vectors, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(vectors), Write(label1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight a single vector rotating
        rotating_vec = vectors[0]
        label2 = Text("Rotation", font_size=20, color=COLOR_2)
        label2.next_to(rotating_vec, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(rotating_vec, angle=PI/2, about_point=rotating_vec.get_start()),
            FadeIn(label2),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash all vectors simultaneously for final impact
        label3 = Text("System", font_size=20, color=COLOR_3)
        label3.next_to(vectors, DOWN)
        
        self.play(
            vectors.animate.set_color(COLOR_3),
            FadeIn(label3),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(vectors))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or beginners in STEM

sections.title: What is a Vector? (Intuitive Concept)
sections.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast with 'scalars' (magnitude only) using a visual arrow representation on a 2D coordinate plane.
sections.example: A squirrel running 5 meters (magnitude) North-East (direction) from its tree.

sections.title: Visualizing Vector Addition
sections.content: Introduce the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Explain how connecting the end of one vector to the start of another creates a resultant vector, emphasizing that order does not change the result (Commutative Property).
sections.example: A drone flies 3 units right, then 4 units up; the resultant vector is the direct diagonal path from start to finish.

sections.title: The Components of a Vector
sections.content: Break down vectors into 'x' and 'y' components (Basis vectors i and j). Use a grid system to show how any vector can be expressed as a linear combination of these basis units.
sections.example: Representing a character's velocity in a game: v = 3i + 2j, where 3 is the horizontal speed and 2 is the vertical jump speed.

sections.title: Scaling Vectors (Scalar Multiplication)
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without altering its direction (unless the scalar is negative). Use animation to show the arrow stretching or shrinking.
sections.example: A robotic arm extending its reach: multiplying the 'direction' vector by 2 to make it twice as long.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Recap: Vectors represent movement and physical properties. Close with a summary of how these concepts form the bedrock of physics engines in games and coordinate navigation.
sections.example: Using vectors to calculate the trajectory of an angry bird aimed at a target structure.
